chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from Muhammad ibn Humran and Jamil ibn Darraj, both of them from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Whenever the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) sent out a military expedition, he would call its commander, seat him by his side, and seat his companions before him; then say: 'March in the name of God, and with God, and in the way of God, and upon the religion of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family). Do not be treacherous, do not steal from the spoils, do not mutilate, and do not cut down a tree unless you are compelled to. Do not kill a decrepit old man, nor a child, nor a woman.' And whichever man, from the lowest to the most excellent of the Muslims, grants protection to any of the polytheists, he is under protection until he hears the word of God. When he hears the word of God, Mighty and Majestic: if he follows you, he is your brother in your religion; and if he refuses, seek God's assistance against him and deliver him to his place of safety.
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), similarly, except that he said:
And whichever man from the Muslims grants protection to a man from the polytheists — whether in the farthest part of the army or its nearest — he is under protection.

key_terms.جار: Jar — one who has been granted temporary protection (aman); inviolable until he reaches safety
key_terms.سريّة: Sariyya — a military expedition or detachment sent without the Prophet personally leading it
key_terms.غلول: Ghulul — treacherous appropriation of war booty before its distribution; a grave sin
key_terms.كلام الله: Kalam Allah — the word/speech of God (i.e., the Quran), recitation of which gives the person a chance to accept Islam
key_terms.مأمن: Ma'man — place of safety/security to which an enemy combatant must be escorted if he declines Islam
key_terms.مثلة: Muthla — mutilation of a corpse; strictly prohibited in Islamic law
key_terms.مِلَّة: Millah — religion, creed, or religious community

ai.seo_question: What instructions did the Prophet Muhammad give before sending a military expedition according to Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith records Imam al-Sadiq's (AS) transmission of the Prophet's (SAWW) standing orders when dispatching military expeditions. The Prophet would personally brief the commander, emphasizing divine authorization for the mission while enumerating strict prohibitions: no treachery, no looting, no mutilation, no destruction of trees, and no killing of non-combatants (the elderly, children, and women). A second chain via Ali ibn Ibrahim provides a slightly variant wording. These instructions reflect the Islamic laws of war (jihad rulings) and show that even the humblest Muslim soldier could grant temporary safe-passage (aman) to an enemy until that person heard the Quran recited.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Muhammad Bin Humran, and Jameel Bin Darraj, all of them, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Whenever Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> sent a battallion, called its commander and made him sit by his<sup>saww</sup> side, and his companions to sit in front of him<sup>asws</sup>. Then he<sup>saww</sup> would say: ‘March in the Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and with Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and in the Way of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and upon the Religion of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>. Neither be treacherous, nor commit excesses, nor mutilate, nor cut down a tree except if you are desperate to it, and do not kill a dying elder, nor a child, nor a woman. 
And whichever man from the lowest of the Muslims and their most superior of them pities anyone from the Polytheists, so he is a neighbour (friend) until he hears the Speech of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>. So when he hears the Speech of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic and if he follows you, so he is your brother in your Religion, and if he refuses, so seek Assistance of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> against him, and deliver him to his safety’.
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, similar to it except that he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘And whichever man from the Muslims pities a man from the Polytheists in the remoteness of the army and its lowest, so he is a neighbour (friend)’.
en.sarwar: 9. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Washsha’ from Muhammad ibn Humran and Jamil ibn al-Darraj who both have narrated who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

whenever the Messenger of Allah dispatched a small group for an armed expedition, he called their commander and made him sit on his side. He then called the soldiers and made them sit in front of him and said to them, ‘March in the name of Allah, with Allah, in the way of Allah and upon the religion of the Messenger of Allah. You must not betray and you must not act excessively, you must not deform people, you must not cut down trees unless you are forced, you must not kill old people, children and women. If anyone of the Muslims of a higher or lower position looks with sympathy upon any of the pagans, such pagan person is in his protection until he hears the words of Allah. When he, the pagan man, hears the words of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, and if he follows you, he then is considered your brother in religion and if he refused, then ask Allah for assistance against him and send him back to his safe place.’”
Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Jamil from abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, a similar Hadith. Except that he has said,
“If anyone of the Muslims looks on a pagan man with sympathy in the near or far away positions of the army, such pagan man is considered under his protection.”
